pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Matter? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Matter.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Matter.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Matter.

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Removing all vegetation

3. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. watt (W)

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Heat.

5. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Decomposers only

6. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Milk souring
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Paper burning to ash

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 100 °C

8. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Light.

10. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only water vapour

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Conservation.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Water Conservation.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Conservation.

12. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

13. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Heating until a solid melts

14. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
15. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
